haiku-low.q1: It rejects and lists the malformed events, accepts the rest, and returns 202 only after the log confirms the write with replication (quorum).
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off from 1 second up to 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The first copy in log order, the winner, is loaded into events_clean. Later copies are duplicates and never reach the warehouse.
haiku-low.q4: Day D is the UTC day of received_at, so it belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is never used.
haiku-low.q5: In the key-value store, one key per event_id, holding the winner's received_at and the copy's ingest sequence. An 8-day TTL removes old entries.
haiku-low.q6: Dedup retries the same copy with backoff, never skips or guesses, and later copies in that partition wait. The lag alarm fires; the log holds the copies.
haiku-low.q7: Dedup commits its offset only after the decided topic accepts, so a re-read returns the same winner. The loader may re-append its last batch; no design makes that idempotent. The close check alerts the operator.
haiku-low.q8: A replay reads archive files for received day D, including duplicates and decisions. It writes rebuilt rows to the staging table events_clean_rebuild_D, which dashboards cannot see, before an atomic swap.
haiku-low.q9: It uses the decision recorded in each archived copy at live time, keeping winners whose received day is D. It fails if any event_id repeats among them. Earlier-day winners are in the earlier day's archive.
haiku-low.q10: The live partition is left untouched and the failure is reported. What happens to the staging table after a failed validation or swap is NOT STATED; the operator recovery steps are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Only days with a closed-day manifest, no replay lock held, and an archive that will not expire (D+90) before the replay can finish.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. The plan does not choose between dropping suspected bot traffic and keeping it with a flag. The archive keeps all events for 90 days either way.

sonnet.q1: It validates each event separately and rejects malformed ones (listed by index and reason, not stored). Valid events are appended to the log; it returns 202 only after the log confirms the write with replication (quorum). If no event is valid it still returns 202 with just the rejections. If the append fails or times out it returns 503 for the whole batch.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off from 1 second up to 5 minutes. The mobile SDK keeps unacknowledged events in an on-device buffer for up to 7 days.
sonnet.q3: The first copy in log order (the winner) is the one loaded into events_clean. Later copies are duplicates: archived but never enriched or loaded. This holds as long as the later copy arrives within the 8-day key TTL.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's partition (day D is the UTC day of received_at, 00:10 Tuesday). The client timestamp is never used. Its replay is the Tuesday replay.
sonnet.q5: In the key-value store, one key per event_id, written only by the dedup stage with an atomic set-if-absent. The value is {winner received_at, ingest sequence of this copy}. Entries expire by TTL after 8 days (7-day client retry window plus 1-day margin).
sonnet.q6: The dedup consumer does not skip or guess. It retries the same copy with backoff and does not move on to later copies in that partition. The lag alarm fires. Meanwhile the collector keeps accepting events into the log, which holds them for 14 days.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED for this exact case as worded. The document says the loader commits its offset only after the append succeeds, and topics keep rows up to 14 days. But loader restart is an open question: after a crash it may re-append its last batch, no idempotent append is designed yet, and a duplicate row would make the close check fail and alert the operator. So double-counting is not avoided by the design today.
sonnet.q8: It reads the archive files for received day D, including duplicates and their recorded decisions (read-only). It does not read the log or events_late. Rebuilt events are written to the staging table events_clean_rebuild_D, which dashboards cannot see.
sonnet.q9: It does not recompute dedup. It uses the decisions recorded in the archive sidecars: it keeps records with decision winner and received day D, sorted by ingest sequence. A duplicate received on day D whose winner was on an earlier day is recorded as duplicate and is not kept. The winner's day is its own received day, so a day-D winner is kept. If any event_id appears more than once among the kept winners, the replay fails.
sonnet.q10: The live partition is untouched (the swap is atomic, so dashboards see the old day), and the failure is reported. What happens to the staging table events_clean_rebuild_D after a failed replay is not set (open question). Recovery steps for the operator are not specified beyond that. Presumably the operator can submit a new replay request (requests are checked against the manifest, lock and archive expiry), but that is not explicitly stated.
sonnet.q11: Closed days only: day D must have a closed-day manifest (check passed after 02:00 UTC on D+1). Also no other replay of D may be running (replay lock), and the archive for D must not expire before the replay finishes (expires at D+90).
sonnet.q12: Not decided. Whether to drop or keep with a flag is an open question. The plan reserves an enrichment step with no default behaviour. The archive keeps all accepted events for 90 days either way.
